speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: how long have you noticed this neck swelling, and has it been growing rapidly? Also, have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant concern given your history of colon cancer; could this neck swelling be a metastasis? Have you noticed any lumps in your armpits or groin, or any changes in your bowel habits recently? Also, is the swelling hard and fixed to the skin, or does it feel soft and mobile?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Cervical Lymph Nodes.

REQUEST TEST: Cervical Ultrasound with Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) of the lymph node.
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound image of the neck swelling.
